newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

TOP STORIES - Education Minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol says he believes the opposition's attacks on his controversial funding of members of parliament's surveys on rural schools are intended to undermine his educational reform plan. An opposition MP, meanwhile, says it is likely that the Democrat Party will campaign to remove the minister. (THE NATION)

- The Expressway and Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (ETA) will suffer most from the government's plan to cut public spending. About half of the agency's planned investment expenditure, including the Bang Khunthien-Samut Sakhon expressway project approved by the previous government, will be suspended. The government has proposed that public spending be cut by 99 billion baht, or two percent of the gross domestic product, in a bid to heal the ailing economy. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- About 20 heads of cattle from Burma, some of which may be infected with anthrax, have been quietly moved out of a Muslim community in defiance of an order issued by city health officials raising fears that the disease may spread. It is not known where the animals are moved to or whether they have been slaughtered and their meat sold to meat markets in the city. (BANGKOK POST) + + + +

- Thailand will allow foreign countries to participate in the operation of international telephone, telex, telegraph and facsimile services under its plan for liberalisation. The commitment to the World Trade Organisation improves an earlier offer that will let foreigners participate only in domestic telephone operations. The liberalisation will be carried out over three years after the new communication bills have been approved by parliament. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Sahaviriya Group has signed a 60-year concession contract with the Lao government to invest in a major railway project with a total length of 1,500 kilometres - a system that will link the land-locked country with Thailand, southern China, Cambodia and Vietnam. The concession is renewable for another 30 years. (THE NATION)

- With the awarding of telecom concessions slowing down from last year's frenetic pace, United Communication Industry Plc is now setting its sights on the broadcasting business. The telecom giant is planning to join the race for new television licences this year. The firm has completed a set of deals to take over 40 radio stations and a private news agency. (THE NATION)
